story_type: spacecraft abort, drop and parachute tests
hook: This rocket blew apart under an Apollo capsule. That was the test.
narration: This rocket blew apart under a prototype Apollo capsule, and that was the test.
Before anyone flew to the Moon, every piece of Apollo had to pass severe tests.
First, engineers dropped the capsule into water, to prove it was seaworthy.
Then the abort test. The tower on the nose is a small rocket that yanks the capsule off a failing booster.
The capsule was pulled from an exploding rocket, and its parachutes had to open on the way down.
Prototypes rode rockets into space to test the flight equipment.
[short pause] Then the service module engine rammed a capsule back into the atmosphere at twenty-five thousand miles an hour, to test the heat shield.
outcome: The scorched capsule came home in one piece, lifted out of the sea.
title: Apollo capsule tested the hard way
description:
Before Apollo flew crews to the Moon, NASA dropped prototype capsules into water, pulled them off exploding rockets, tested their parachutes and sent one back into the atmosphere at 25,000 miles an hour to test the heat shield.

facts.claim: Capsule drop tests into water for seaworthiness
facts.source_quote: The command module or crew compartment was subjected to drop tests to assure the seaworthiness of the craft.

facts.claim: Abort tests pulled the capsule from an exploding rocket; parachute tests
facts.source_quote: And abort tests, at which the launch escape system pulled the capsule from an exploding rocket. Parachute tests --
Prototypes of the various modules were launched into space, to test flight equipment.
The main engine of the service module was fired to ram the command module back into the earth's atmosphere at 25,000 miles an hour, to test the heat shield.
